To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the microtubule cytoskeleton plays an important role in determining the locomotory pattern of macrophages.
the microtubule cytoskeleton plays a critical role in the control of cell shape and locomotion.
microtubules normally inhibit the flow of cytoplasm in the cell cortex and that microfilaments are the contractile elements that produce this flow when the microtubules are absent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the microtubule system in cellular locomotion and the possible role of the microfilament system in ameboid locomotion.
the effects of microtubule-disrupting drugs on the cytoarchitecture of cultured mouse peritoneal macrophones and the resulting alterations in cellular locomotion.
the effects of colchicine on the locomotion of macrophages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the drug-induced microtubule disruption leads to a shift in locomotor form from gliding to ameboid.
microtubules are not essential for locomotion of the macrophage, but are necessary for maintenance of normal cytoplasmic polarity and for the gliding type of locomotion.
colchicine and vinblastine cause a shift in cellular movement from gliding to ameboid, and that this shift in movement is due to a change in cortical cytoplasmic structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
colchicine or other microtubule inhibitors can induce ameboid movement in macrophages, and that the microfilament system of these cells is responsible for the observed cytoplasmic flow.
the microtubule system of the cytoplams is essential in the regulation of the cytoplamic streaming and that the streaming itself is essential for the gliding form of cell locomotion.

the interphase microfilament array is a contractile structure that is normally opposed by an opposing array of interphase microturbules; in the absence or inactivation of this opposing array, the microfilament array contracts to cause cytoplasmic movement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microtubule-dependent cell locomotion is not a requirement for cell motility.
cytoskeletal structures are important in maintaining the normal form of locomotion of cultured macrophages.
the cytoskeletal structure is not just a static scaffolding for the cell, but rather is actively involved in the control of cell shape and locomotion.
